_comment: Raw vertical cut: 1080x1920, full-frame speaker, one text hook pinned to the top of the frame for the opening seconds, bold burned-in captions, and nothing else. No lower thirds, no B-roll, no region split. The format exists because the polished version of this footage performs worse than the unpolished one.
_usage: Project.create(root, slug, preset) deep-merges this over the skeleton in vedit/project.py: dicts merge, lists replace wholesale, project_id / created_utc / schema_version / _computed are dropped. Keys beginning with '_' are documentation and MUST be ignored by consumers.
name: tiktok-raw
description: 9:16 raw cut. Full-frame speaker, text hook at the top, bold captions, no graphics.
_comment_loudnorm: Copied from presets/platforms.json -> tiktok.loudnorm and frozen into the project on creation, so a later edit to platforms.json cannot silently re-target an already-mastered video. QC check (f) measures the master against THIS block.
_comment_cut_profile: See presets/cut-profiles.json. Note 'aggressive' still flags rather than removes German modal particles - CONTRACT section 8 makes that unconditional, and on raw vertical material the particles are most of what makes it sound like a person.
_comment_captions: ON, always - the feed autoplays muted. WhisperX runs with --suppress_numerals, so numerals arrive spelled out ('zwanzig', not '20'); correct them with captions.overrides entries rather than by re-transcribing.

layout._comment: One region. The hook is an overlay on top of it, not a region split - the speaker keeps the whole frame and the hook sits over the head-room above them.

speaker._comment_crop_bias: Bias upward so the face sits above centre and leaves the bottom third to the captions.

layout._comment_graphics_mode: No graphics lane for this format. If a shot needs a diagram it is the wrong format - use shortform-explainer.
layout._comment_captions_region: null = the tiktok-bold preset's own margins decide, and those come straight from platforms.tiktok.caption_safe_area_pct.

hook._comment: A single text card pinned near the top of the frame for the opening beat. The story stage writes the actual line into overlays[] as a normal overlay record anchored to {segment_id: <first enabled segment>, offset_frames: 0} - this block is only the shape and the styling it should use.
hook._comment_template: Must be a pure function of ?t=<seconds> - no CSS animations, no requestAnimationFrame. That is what makes the Chrome screenshot lane deterministic and therefore cacheable.
hook._comment_duration: 90 frames = 3.0 s at 30 fps. Long enough to read twice, short enough to be gone before the payoff.
hook._comment_region: y 10 % clears platforms.tiktok.safe_area_pct.top (8 %) with a little margin. Width 88 % is fine at this height: the action rail does not start until roughly 55 % down the frame.

props._comment_text: Empty on creation. The story stage fills it - and it is the single highest-leverage string in the whole document.

hook._comment_font: The hook is rendered by Chrome from HTML, not by libass, so it loads the file with @font-face from a file:/// URL. The family string still matches the ASS Fontname so the hook and the captions are visibly the same typeface.
